takeaways: Global central banks (BoJ, Fed, ECB, BoE) maintained policy rates but signaled persistent inflation risks and a 'higher for longer' outlook, driving U.S. Treasury yields to multi-year highs (30-year >5%) primarily due to rising real yields, making bonds increasingly attractive and potentially impacting risk assets.

The AI boom continues to fuel unprecedented investment, with hyperscalers committing over $1 trillion to AI infrastructure, custom silicon, and data centers, driving record earnings for tech giants like Microsoft and Amazon while simultaneously leading to capacity constraints and rising memory costs. This also signals a strategic pivot by AI labs towards proprietary product development, intensifying competition.

Asia presents a bifurcated economic picture: China faces structural headwinds from private sector deleveraging and weak domestic demand, pointing to slower, government-led growth, while Hong Kong's retail and commercial property markets are experiencing a robust recovery, attracting significant foreign investment and seeing rising rents, signaling renewed confidence.

items.title: Bank of Japan keeps rates steady, warns on inflation
bullets: The BOJ maintained its short-term interest rate at 1% but issued a stronger warning that underlying inflation risks exceeding its 2% target, signaling potential future rate hikes.

Inflationary pressures are attributed to robust global AI demand and rising medium/long-term inflation expectations, with receding concerns over the Middle East conflict allowing a focus on domestic price risks.
Despite a hawkish statement and government yen-buying intervention, the yen remained weak near ¥160.760/USD, while the 2-year JGB yield rose, reflecting market anticipation of further tightening.
items.reason: Significant hawkish shift from a major central bank with global market implications.

items.title: Three Central Banks Hold Rates Steady – Here’s What’s Driving Their Caution
bullets: The U.S. Federal Reserve, European Central Bank, and Bank of Japan all maintained policy rates, balancing persistent inflation above target with concerns over slowing economic growth.

Policymakers are assessing the lagged effects of previous hikes and are wary of overtightening, while still facing risks from supply chain disruptions, geopolitical tensions, and volatile commodity prices.
The collective pause implies continued elevated borrowing costs for businesses and households, with future policy decisions remaining data-dependent amidst an uncertain global economic landscape.
items.reason: Provides a crucial overview of major central bank policy and rationale.

items.title: Gold prices going nowhere in a hurry as BoE leaves rates unchanged
bullets: The Bank of England held its Bank Rate steady at 3.75%, but three Monetary Policy Committee members unexpectedly voted for a hike, signaling growing internal pressure for tighter policy.
The BoE cited ongoing volatility in crude and refined energy prices due to Middle East events as a key inflation driver, acknowledging the uncertain impact on the UK economy.
Despite the hawkish split, the gold market showed little reaction, as the broader global trend towards higher interest rates continues to increase the opportunity cost of holding the precious metal.
items.reason: Specific central bank action with notable dissent and impact on a key commodity.

items.title: Microsoft's $450 billion one-day surge tops Turkey's entire stock market as Azure hits $100B milestone
bullets: Microsoft's market value surged by an unprecedented $450 billion in one day, reaching $3.4 trillion, driven by better-than-expected earnings and robust AI product performance.
Q2 revenue hit $90 billion (+18% YoY) with profits up 31%, fueled by over 30 million paid seats for Microsoft 365 Copilot and a nearly one-third jump in Intelligent Cloud AI revenue.
Azure cloud computing platform revenue surpassed $100 billion for FY26, validating Microsoft's AI strategy while capital expenditures came in slightly below expectations ($41B vs $42B).
items.reason: Unprecedented market value surge for a mega-cap, validating the AI investment thesis and setting new benchmarks.

items.title: Stocks Rise on Big Amazon Earnings Beat: Stock Market Today
bullets: Major equity indexes (Dow +0.5%, S&P 500 +0.7%, Nasdaq +1.0%) ended Friday higher, snapping weekly losing streaks despite market volatility.
Treasury yields surged to their highest levels since 2007, with the 10-year yield climbing 4.9 basis points to 4.712% and the 30-year bond yield reaching 5.253%.
Cleveland and Minneapolis Fed Presidents Hammack and Kashkari advocated for immediate rate hikes to combat inflation, indicating a hawkish stance despite the Fed's recent hold.
items.reason: Significant macro drivers (yields, Fed hawkishness) impacting overall market sentiment and future policy expectations.

items.title: US Treasury yields rise as TIPS challenge the inflation narrative
bullets: 30-year Treasury yields reached their highest level since 2007, with the 2-year yield rising 76 basis points since early March, indicating a multi-month bond sell-off.

Despite mainstream attributing rising yields to inflation from energy prices, 5-year TIPS inflation expectations are trending down to 2.2% since May, suggesting rising real yields are the primary driver.
Markets are pricing in a 63% probability of a September Fed rate hike, and government bonds are now more profitable than crypto cash-and-carry trades for the first time since 2019.
items.reason: Provides critical insights into bond market drivers, challenging the prevailing inflation narrative with TIPS data, and highlighting Fed expectations.

items.title: Why spiking U.S. bond yields could be a big warning for the economy
bullets: The 30-year U.S. Treasury yield climbed above 5% (around 5.25%), reaching its highest level since 2007, following the Fed's "higher for longer" signal.
Elevated yields make bonds an attractive, low-risk alternative, potentially drawing capital away from riskier assets like stocks, real estate, and business investment.
This sharp rise signals market concerns about inflation, government debt, or economic uncertainty, leading to higher borrowing costs for consumers (mortgages) and businesses.
items.reason: Explains the macro implications of rising long-term yields for the economy, borrowing costs, and asset allocation.

items.title: China’s debt ratio dips. Why it may not bode well for the economy
bullets: China's overall debt-to-GDP ratio decreased by 1.1 percentage points to 308.2% in Q2, primarily due to deleveraging by households and firms, not robust economic growth.
Household debt-to-GDP ratio fell 1.3 percentage points to 57.7%, with mortgage lending shrinking for 13 consecutive quarters and consumer lending decline accelerating to 1.8% from 0.2%.

The private sector contraction, evidenced by reduced borrowing and investment, indicates the government is becoming the sole driver of growth, masking underlying economic weakness despite nominal GDP growth of 5.9%.
items.reason: Highlights critical structural deleveraging in private sector, signaling fundamental economic shifts and potential long-term growth challenges.

items.title: China: Consumption pivot points to slower growth - Rabobank
bullets: China's Q2 GDP growth of 4.3% YoY undershot expectations (4.5% YoY), driven by persistent weak domestic demand and a deepening real estate crisis.
Rabobank anticipates Beijing will implement renewed consumption subsidies and two minor 10bp PBoC rate cuts to stimulate demand, but doubts a sustainable recovery in consumer sentiment.

The necessary transition from an investment/export-led model to a consumption-driven economy is projected to result in structurally lower GDP growth, with forecasts of 4.5% for 2026 and 4.2% for 2027, below China's official target range.
items.reason: Provides a critical analyst perspective on China's growth trajectory, policy responses, and the long-term implications of its economic rebalancing.

items.title: Swire Properties posts double-digit retail growth in mainland China, 100pc HK mall occupancy
bullets: Hong Kong retail sector shows robust recovery, with Swire's malls maintaining 100% occupancy and boosted sales from tourist arrivals (e.g., Labor Day Golden Week) and strong luxury goods demand.

Mainland China retail performance is exceptionally strong, with Taikoo Li Sanlitun and HKRI Taikoo Hui recording over 60% and 80% year-on-year retail sales growth, driven by premium brand flagships and festive events.
Office leasing sentiment improved in Q2, with Pacific Place and Taikoo Place occupancy rising to 98% and 90% respectively, indicating a strengthening commercial property market.
items.reason: Comprehensive positive performance from a major developer across retail, office, and residential sectors in both HK and mainland China, signaling strong economic recovery and consumer confidence.

items.title: Singapore-based investors now the top non-local buyers of Hong Kong office assets
bullets: Singaporean investors became the largest non-local buyers of HK commercial properties in Q2 2026, investing HK$3.37 billion (62% of total non-local/mainland investment), indicating renewed foreign confidence.
This capital inflow is driven by significant price corrections (up to 50% decline) in HK office assets, presenting an opportunity for long-term recovery and discounted acquisitions.
Hong Kong's Grade-A office rents in Central rose 7.3% in H1, the largest six-month increase in 15 years, with vacancy rates falling to 8.8%, signaling a strong rebound in the prime office market.
items.reason: Highlights significant foreign capital investment into a key HK asset class (office property) driven by attractive valuations and coinciding with a strong recovery in prime office rents and occupancy.

items.title: Amazon Completes $50 Billion Investment in OpenAI
bullets: Amazon finalized its $50 billion investment in OpenAI, completing the remaining $21.3 billion after June 30, following earlier tranches of $15 billion and $13.7 billion.

The deal designates Amazon Web Services (AWS) as the exclusive third-party cloud provider for OpenAI's Frontier program, with potential infrastructure agreements totaling $100 billion over eight years.

OpenAI's ChatGPT is approaching 1 billion weekly active users, making it one of the fastest-growing apps, while the company simultaneously cut prices and improved performance for some models to enhance enterprise value.
items.reason: Direct financial transaction, strategic cloud partnership, and significant user growth for a leading AI product.

items.title: When Artificial Intelligence Is Too Valuable To Sell
bullets: Frontier AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are likely to shift from licensing their core models via API to developing and selling proprietary products built atop these models, driven by increased competition.

The proliferation of advanced AI models from 5-7 major players (e.g., Google, Meta, SpaceX) is commoditizing raw model access, shifting profit capture towards specialized AI products and underlying compute infrastructure.

This strategic pivot implies a 'pull up the ladder' approach, where leading labs use their cutting-edge models to create unique products, potentially intensifying competition with existing software clients and redefining value accrual in the AI ecosystem.
items.reason: Discusses a fundamental shift in AI business models and competitive strategy with broad market implications.

items.title: How Alphabet and Amazon Each Built The ‘Best’ Nvidia Chip Alternatives
bullets: Alphabet's custom TPUs drove an 82% surge in Google Cloud, boosting operating margin from 20.7% to 35.6% in Q2 FY2026, demonstrating the cost efficiency of in-house silicon.
Amazon's AI and Chips businesses (Trainium, Graviton) exceeded a $25 billion annual revenue run rate with triple-digit growth, contributing to AWS's $42.23 billion revenue and 39.4% operating margin.

Both tech giants are making substantial CapEx investments (Alphabet $195-205B, Amazon ~$200B) into their custom silicon, indicating a long-term strategic shift to reduce reliance on external suppliers like Nvidia.
items.reason: Highlights a major competitive threat and strategic shift by Nvidia's largest customers, impacting long-term market dynamics.

items.title: Prediction: Nvidia Will Be a $10 Trillion Company by 2030. Here's the Math.
bullets: Nvidia needs to more than double its current ~$4.7 trillion market cap by 2030, requiring an 18% annualized return to reach $10 trillion, assuming a stable share count.
Achieving a $10 trillion valuation would necessitate $333 billion in net profit at a 30x P/E, significantly up from fiscal 2026's $120 billion on $216 billion revenue (56% margin).

Analysts project Nvidia's revenue to grow at an annualized 32% from $393 billion (FY27) to $688 billion (FY29), with a 50% net margin on FY29 revenue yielding $344 billion profit, supporting the $10.3 trillion target.
items.reason: Provides a detailed financial roadmap and assumptions for the market leader's future valuation, crucial for investor outlook.

items.title: Global sales of electric cars reached record levels in 50 countries
bullets: Global EV sales rebounded sharply in Q2 2026, rising 35% compared to Q1, reaching record levels in 50 countries, notably doubling in Australia, Brazil, India, Korea, and Vietnam year-on-year.
The surge is attributed to the energy crisis and Mideast war, which drove fuel price volatility, making EVs a key energy security solution for oil-importing nations.
IEA projects EVs to comprise 29% of total global car sales in 2026, with China's H1 2026 EV exports nearly matching its total 2025 exports, indicating strong international market penetration.
items.reason: Provides comprehensive global market data, growth drivers, and future projections critical for investment strategy.

items.title: EV prices aren't following the 'law of used cars,' analyst says — what it means for buyers and sellers
bullets: Used EV prices are appreciating, contrary to the typical depreciation trend, with Recurrent reporting a 7% YTD increase through mid-July 2026 and Edmunds noting a 6% rise for 3-year-old EVs in H1 2026.
This unusual appreciation, affecting 21 of 25 top-selling used EV models, benefits current owners by improving resale values but could deter new buyers due to higher entry costs.
The shift is attributed to changes in supply and demand patterns, impacting residual values for financial institutions and potentially influencing new EV sales strategies.
items.reason: Highlights a significant, counter-intuitive market trend with direct financial implications for EV asset valuation and consumer behavior.

items.title: Amazon Lifts 2026 AI Capex to $220B, Still Capacity-Constrained
bullets: Amazon increased its 2026 AI infrastructure capital expenditure forecast by $20 billion to $220 billion, primarily due to higher memory costs, indicating intense competition for critical AI components.

Despite this massive investment, CEO Andy Jassy projects AI capacity will remain constrained through 2027, with contracted demand already extending into 2028, signaling sustained high demand and potential pricing power for data center services.

AWS achieved its fastest growth in 18 quarters, with revenue climbing 36.7% year-over-year to $42.2 billion, and its AI and custom silicon businesses now operate at a combined $25 billion annual revenue run rate.
items.reason: Direct, quantifiable, market-moving data from a hyperscaler on AI capex and capacity constraints.

items.title: Big tech spends more than $1 trillion on AI infrastructure — additional $745 billion expected to be added to the figure in 2026 alone
bullets: Amazon, Google, Meta, and Microsoft have collectively spent $1.1 trillion on AI infrastructure since 2023, with an additional $745 billion projected for 2026, signaling an unprecedented, sustained investment cycle in the sector.

This massive power demand is forcing U.S. utility companies to invest billions in grid upgrades, with costs potentially passed to consumers, as exemplified by Oregon's POWER Act increasing bills for large data center users by 30%.
Hyperscalers' high liquidity is driving up prices for HBM memory chips, leading manufacturers like Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix to prioritize these lucrative AI components over traditional DRAM.
items.reason: Broad overview of hyperscaler AI capex and its significant, multi-sector financial implications (utilities, semiconductors, regulatory).

items.title: FAA Proposes Faster Licensing Process for Commercial Space Industry
bullets: The FAA proposes streamlining commercial space licensing by waiving environmental review requirements from 13 federal laws, aiming to reduce costs and delays for launch operators.
This regulatory shift is intended to accelerate commercial space activity, strengthen the U.S. competitive position, and support a sector that authorized a record 204 operations in FY2025.

The move addresses the rapid growth in commercial space, with more operations authorized in the last five years than the previous three decades combined, indicating significant market expansion potential.
items.reason: Federal regulatory change directly reducing costs and accelerating growth for the entire commercial space industry.

items.title: Byron Donalds launches ‘Space Race’ policy rocket
bullets: Gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds proposes 'permit at warp speed' and identifying 10 strategic development sites to establish Florida as a global space manufacturing hub.
The plan includes 'zero-tuition training programs' and an Office for Space Industry to foster workforce readiness and attract companies, aiming to create thousands of high-paying jobs.

Donalds projects Florida's annual rocket launches to exceed 1,000 in coming years (up from 165 in 2025), contributing to an anticipated $1.8 trillion in economic activity in the space sector over the next decade.
items.reason: Ambitious state-level policy proposals with substantial economic targets and direct benefits for space companies in Florida.
